tagline.text: Juan Tomás’s wife.

description.text: Juan Tomás’s wife, who crowds into Kino’s doorway with her children after the scorpion sting.
When Kino’s house burns, she mourns his family as dead, until they turn up at her door. She helps keep them hidden.

tagline.text: Kino and Juana’s baby son, stung by a scorpion.
The baby whose future Kino dreams the pearl will buy.
Kino and Juana’s son, killed by a tracker’s shot.

description.text: Kino and Juana’s infant son, who sleeps in a hanging box. A scorpion stings him on the shoulder, and the doctor refuses to treat him.
The swelling begins to go down after Juana’s poultice.
Kino dreams of sending him to school so he can read and be free. After the doctor gives him a white powder, he falls sick, and the doctor then “cures” him.
While hiding in a cave, he cries out; a tracker mistakes the sound for a coyote and fires, killing him.

moments.text: Was stung by a scorpion.
Fell ill after the doctor’s powder.
Was killed by a rifle shot fired toward his cry.

tagline.text: Kino’s older brother.
Kino’s brother, a cautious adviser.
Kino’s brother, who hides the family when they must flee.

description.text: Kino’s older brother, who crowds into Kino’s doorway with his family after the scorpion stings Coyotito.
He stands beside Kino as the neighbours gather to hear what the pearl will buy.
Wiser in the ways of the world, he warns Kino that men who have gone to sell pearls in the capital have disappeared, and that he is defying the whole way of life in the town. Still, he supports him.
He risks his own safety to hide Kino’s family for a day, gathers supplies for them and helps them escape at night.

moments.text: Warned Kino of the dangers of going to the capital.
Hid Kino’s family in his house.

tagline.text: Kino’s strong, devoted wife.
Kino’s wife, who fears the pearl is evil.
A mother in mourning, who will not take the pearl back.

description.text: Kino’s wife and Coyotito’s mother. Patient and practical, she acts fast when the scorpion strikes, sucking the poison from the wound and insisting they go to the doctor. Kino marvels at her strength.
She treats Coyotito with a seaweed poultice and prays for Kino to find a pearl.
After the night attack she begs Kino to destroy the pearl, convinced it is evil and will destroy their family.
She stands by Kino’s decision, though she is afraid.
She tries to throw the pearl into the sea and is beaten for it, but does not turn against Kino. When he kills a man, she decides that they must flee together.
She hides with Coyotito in a cave while Kino attacks the trackers. After Coyotito is killed, she walks back to town beside Kino, carrying her son, and refuses the pearl when Kino offers it to her.

moments.text: Sucked the scorpion’s poison from Coyotito’s shoulder.
Treated Coyotito with a seaweed poultice.
Begged Kino to throw the pearl away.
Tried to throw the pearl into the sea.
Refused the pearl when Kino offered it to her.

tagline.text: A poor native pearl diver, content with his family.
The diver who finds the Pearl of the World.
A diver whose pearl brings dreams, and danger.
A man defying the pearl buyers and the town.
A man on the run after killing an attacker.
A grieving father who gives the pearl back to the sea.

description.text: A young pearl diver who lives with his wife, Juana, and baby son, Coyotito, in a brush hut by the sea. He hears his people’s old songs in his head: the Song of the Family when all is well, the Song of Evil when danger comes. When the doctor refuses to treat his son, his helpless anger at the people who have long looked down on his race boils over.
A skilled diver who owns little except his canoe, inherited from his grandfather. He finds an enormous, perfect pearl.

The pearl awakens his ambitions: a church wedding, new clothes, a rifle and, most of all, an education for Coyotito. He grows suspicious of everyone. Attacked in the night, he refuses Juana’s plea to throw the pearl away, insisting it is their one chance.
He refuses the buyers’ insulting offers and resolves to go to the capital, defying a system that has always kept his people poor. He is frightened, but stubborn and proud.

Obsessed with the pearl, he beats Juana when she tries to throw it away, then kills a man who attacks him. With his canoe destroyed and his house burned, he flees north with his family, saying the pearl has become his soul.
Hunted by trackers, he kills all three, but a rifle shot kills Coyotito. He returns to town with Juana and throws the pearl into the sea.

moments.text: Struck the doctor’s gate after being turned away.
Found the Pearl of the World.
Told his neighbours what the pearl would buy.
Fought off an intruder in the night.
Refused the pearl buyers’ offers and decided to go to the capital.
Beat Juana when she tried to throw the pearl away.
Killed one of the men who attacked him.
Killed the three trackers.
Threw the pearl back into the sea.

tagline.text: Beggars outside the church who know everyone’s business.

description.text: They sit on the church steps and know all about the doctor’s greed and his past. They follow Kino to the doctor’s house to watch.
They are glad to hear about the pearl, hoping Kino will give alms.

tagline.text: A greedy, self-indulgent doctor who refuses to treat poor natives.
The doctor who suddenly wants to treat Coyotito, now that there is a pearl.

description.text: A fat, lazy man from the race that conquered Kino’s people, who longs for his past life in Paris. He refuses to treat Coyotito when Kino can pay only with a few worthless pearls.

When he hears of the pearl, he arrives uninvited, warns that scorpion poison can strike later, and gives Coyotito a powder; the baby falls ill and the doctor returns to “cure” him. Kino suspects him of making the child sick on purpose, and he tries to find out where the pearl is hidden.

moments.text: Refused to treat Coyotito.
Gave Coyotito a powder, then returned to “cure” him.

tagline.text: The doctor’s servant, one of Kino’s own people.

description.text: He belongs to Kino’s race, but refuses to speak their old language at the doctor’s door and turns the family away with the doctor’s lie that he is out.
He accompanies the doctor when the doctor comes uninvited to treat Coyotito.

tagline.text: Kino’s neighbours in the brush houses, always watching.

description.text: They follow Kino’s family to the doctor’s house, curious to see what happens.
They crowd into Kino’s hut to hear his plans and are startled by his boldness.
They walk with Kino to the pearl buyers, and afterwards argue over whether he was right to refuse.

tagline.text: The scorpion that stings Coyotito.

description.text: It creeps down the rope of Coyotito’s box and stings him when he laughs and shakes the rope. Kino crushes it.

moments.text: Stung Coyotito.

tagline.text: The greatest pearl ever found.
A treasure that awakens greed all over town.
A treasure that has cost a life and a home.
Returned to the bottom of the sea.

description.text: A pearl the size of a gull’s egg, perfectly round and glowing, found by Kino in a huge oyster.
Everyone in town begins to scheme over it. To Kino it shows pictures of a better future; to Juana it seems evil.
The buyers call it too big to be valuable, a mere curiosity, but Kino believes it is worth fifty thousand pesos.
Kino says it has become his soul; to keep it he has lost his canoe and his house.
Looking into it after Coyotito’s death, Kino sees only ugliness. He throws it back into the sea.

moments.text: Was found by Kino.
Was appraised at a fraction of its worth by the buyers.
Was thrown back into the sea.

tagline.text: An unseen intruder who comes in the dark for the pearl.
Unknown enemies who have cost Kino his canoe and home.

description.text: Someone creeps into Kino’s hut in the dark and strikes him before escaping. Kino cannot see who it is.
Kino is attacked again outside his hut, this time by more than one figure.
Several men attack Kino on the path; he kills one. Someone smashes his canoe and burns his house. Who sent them remains unknown.

moments.text: Broke into Kino’s hut.
Attacked Kino outside his hut.
Attacked Kino on the path; one was killed.

tagline.text: The town’s pearl dealers, eager for Kino’s pearl.
Dealers who pretend to compete, but try to cheat Kino together.

description.text: When they hear of the pearl, they plan how to get it as cheaply as possible.

They seem to be rivals, but the town believes they all work for one man. The first, who rolls a coin across his knuckles, calls the pearl a worthless curiosity and offers a thousand pesos; the rest offer even less.

moments.text: Offered Kino a fraction of the pearl’s worth.

tagline.text: The town priest, who hopes the pearl will pay for church repairs.

description.text: When he hears about the pearl he thinks of repairs the church needs, then visits Kino to remind him to give thanks to God and to point out that he and Juana were never married in the church.

moments.text: Visited Kino after hearing about the pearl.

tagline.text: Two trackers and a rifleman hunting Kino’s family.

description.text: Two men on foot who read the ground for signs, and a horseman with a rifle. They follow Kino’s family into the mountains and camp by the pool below their hiding place. When Coyotito cries, the rifleman fires at the sound. Kino kills all three.

moments.text: Fired at Coyotito’s cry, killing him.
Were killed by Kino.
